@graph.name: AoU-01: Periodic proof test
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: The end user performs a full proof test of the safety function at intervals not exceeding 12 months, as described in the safety manual.
@graph.rationale: The claimed PFDavg for the SIL 3 safety function is only achieved with this proof-test interval.

@graph.name: AoU-02: De-energize-to-trip wiring
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: Final elements are wired de-energize-to-trip, so that loss of output power results in the process safe state.
@graph.rationale: The logic solver commands the safe state by removing output power; the field wiring must translate that into the physical safe state.

@graph.name: AoU-03: Environmental limits
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: The controller is operated within the specified environmental limits (-25 to +70 C, condensation-free), per the safety manual.
@graph.rationale: Failure rates and diagnostic assumptions in the FMEDA are only valid inside the qualified environment.

@graph.name: AoU-04: SIL of sensors and final elements
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: Field sensors and final elements are selected and maintained to at least the SIL claimed for the overall safety instrumented function.
@graph.rationale: The logic solver contributes only its allocated portion of the SIF's PFDavg.

@graph.name: AoU-05: Configuration by qualified personnel
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: Safety parameters are configured only by personnel trained on the engineering tool, and the configuration is independently verified before commissioning.
@graph.rationale: Systematic configuration faults are controlled by competence and independent review, not by the logic solver alone.

@graph.name: AoU-06: Monitored power supply
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: A monitored, adequately-rated power supply is provided; loss or out-of-tolerance supply is detected and drives the system to the safe state.
@graph.rationale: Power-supply integrity is a precondition for the diagnostics to run.

@graph.name: AoU-07: EMC and surge immunity
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: The installation meets the EMC and surge-immunity assumptions (IEC 61326-3-1) used in the safety analysis.
@graph.rationale: The residual-error-rate calculation of the safety communication layer assumes a bounded bit-error rate.

@graph.name: AoU-08: No defeat of hardware fault tolerance
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: External wiring and installation do not defeat the internal 2oo3 architecture; the recommended channel separation is applied.
@graph.rationale: Common-cause failures could otherwise undermine the HFT=1 claim.

@graph.name: AoU-09: Management of change for updates
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: Firmware is not updated while the safety function is in operation; updates follow the documented management-of-change procedure.
@graph.rationale: Online reprogramming is outside the analysed operational context.

@graph.name: BASE-61508: IEC 61508 compliance baseline
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: The software safety lifecycle conforms to IEC 61508-3:2010 (route 1S), achieving systematic capability SC 3 for a SIL 3 safety function.
@graph.rationale: Establishes the normative development baseline the product claims conformance to.

@graph.name: BASE-MISRA: MISRA C:2012 coding baseline
@graph.functionalsafety_assumptionStatement: Safety-related C code conforms to MISRA C:2012 (Amendment 2), with documented and approved deviations only.
@graph.rationale: Establishes the coding-standard baseline the safety components conform to.
